source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

hinge.title: Decide when an even-area region is still not tileable by 2 x 1 tiles by using a black-and-white coloring invariant.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Black-and-white grid is the label that belongs on this item, so 'Decide when an even-area region is still not tileable by 2 x 1 tiles' is answered as black-and-white grid rather than plain grid.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: plain grid still holds here even though The coloring must alternate so neighboring unit squares have opposite colors is missing from the stem — on the item about Decide when an even-area region is still not tileable.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: The plain grid rule also covers this: rectangular grids with no missing squares, so it is not an exception — on the item about Decide when an even-area region is still not tileable.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: The answer is plain grid because of the visible appearance named in the stem, without using 'Decide when an even-area region is still not tileable by 2 x 1 tiles' as the operative test.

intelligence.enrichment: In a checkerboard coloring of a grid region, every 2 x 1 tile covers one black square and one white square; therefore a region with unequal black and white counts cannot be tiled, even if its total number of squares is even.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 6 Mathematics question. Chapter: math/grade_07/ch_206. The student must decide: Decide when an even-area region is still not tileable by 2 x 1 tiles by using a black-and-white coloring invariant. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Supply exactly one complete tikzpicture. The stem must refer to that figure. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options). Two-tier (choose, then reason) is welcome: put A/B/C on part.options, not typed into part text.
